label: August 1895
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1895 from our dossiers, placed on 1910 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). White press only: our sources hold no Black papers for 1895. Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 58 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1895. They come from the 111 located events in the August 1895 table, which includes July events first reported in August. We did not write dossiers for 31 events that were plainly out of scope from the table alone (white victims, no race given, no one harmed, a legal act, another year), and two more belong to earlier months. Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Twenty-one of the 79 dossiers are set aside. Seven are duplicates folded into another record: two later reports of the Smyrna, Georgia, clash; the July threats against Emmet Divers at Hannibal, Missouri, the start of the pursuit that ended in his lynching; a second record of the threat to Henry Mitchell Smith at Lexington, Kentucky; the Purvis report of the Tom Johnson lynching; and two copies of the dispatch on the Lafayette and Taylor county church raids in Florida. Fourteen are out of scope. Samuel Lewis, lynched at Juno, Florida, was white. Harrison Lewis, lynched at Springfield, Kentucky, was said to have been hanged by Black men for killing a Black man, and the Baxter, Arkansas, whipping was by and of Black people. No report gives anyone’s race at Clarksville, Tennessee, Savannah, or for Kimball Green in Missouri. Four were manhunts or rumors with lynching talk but no mob and no one hurt (Dallas, Little Rock, Des Moines, Fauquier County), the Berryville lynching telegram was denied at Berryville, and three cannot be placed in 1895: the Denmark, South Carolina, lynching told in a humor sketch, the Decatur ministers whipped in an undated editorial anecdote, and a Mexia manhunt from “not many years ago.”

Police violence is kept generously: men shot while fleeing or while a warrant was served, and the militia’s volleys into the Black crowd guarding the Winston, North Carolina, jail, are all included. Only gunfights over a crime in progress are set aside.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched the papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. For 1895 our sources hold no Black press, so every account rests on white papers; clippings are shown as page images where we could place them on the scan, otherwise as text.

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
